summary: Scope component titles are unreadable over patterned fills in dark mode and overflow circular nodes
evidence: User screenshot 2026-09-04 at 3.13.59 PM shows black SVG titles on a dark canvas with high-contrast hatch fills; renderer has no explicit SVG text fill and no bounded title layout

summary: Scope ring coordinates collapse the four-component project into a stack and dependency arrows overlap
evidence: The initial model puts the two first-ring peers at angles 0 and pi and the outer singleton at angle 0; every x coordinate is zero. Reciprocal reliance arrows share a path, and a longer edge passes through the central card.

summary: Scope library preview build confused canonical id data with Cytoscape id method
evidence: npm run build --prefix scripts/scope-preview: TypeError n.id is not a function at layout.mjs:33 while determining disconnected membership.

summary: Scope preview center control exposes a glyph rather than its purpose as its accessible name
evidence: Browser accessibility lookup for button Center gravity timed out; DOM button has title but text content is the glyph, with no aria-label.

summary: Scope library preview renders rings but no component cards or connections in user Safari screenshot
evidence: User Safari screenshot Screenshot 2026-09-04 at 3.48.46 PM shows running app with rings, heading and controls but no cards or edges. Chrome file-open still renders all four cards. Cause not yet established.

summary: The first taxonomy parity test compared a facet ID against its own prefixed ID, producing a false missing-facet result
evidence: Focused test: expected canonical-state question but received undefined; predicate was f.id === facet-prefix plus f.id instead of the frozen fixture facet.id. Other nine taxonomy tests passed.

summary: Existing Scope browser checks use page-wide Journal selectors that collide with the mounted Taxonomy panel
evidence: Chrome offline and WebKit live checks fail strict locator resolution: .empty-reading matches both Journal and Taxonomy. New taxonomy browser checks pass both engines.

summary: Overlapping status writers can lose a successful report or leave unreadable JSON
evidence: node scripts/taxonomy-risk-probes.mjs: sequential atlas-plus-mass control preserved both. Across 20 isolated overlapping trials both writers returned successfully, but 18 final records were unreadable and two were readable with a report missing; none preserved both. Schedule frequencies are one local run, not an incidence estimate.

summary: Calibration counts invalid outcome labels and silently drops torn sample rows
evidence: node scripts/taxonomy-risk-probes.mjs: one valid defect row, one not-an-outcome row and one torn JSON row produce two returned rows, labeled=2 and defectRateWithoutMisses=0.5. Only one row has a valid clean/defect label; surviving damage is not reported by readCalibrationSamples.

summary: A taxonomy candidate can require an operational question that the interview does not expose
evidence: classifyTaxonomy with authority=yes includes validator-type-checker needing signal:validates-rules, but the emitted questions omit validates-rules because representation was not answered yes. Required evidence must make its own question relevant.

summary: The added alternate-entry taxonomy test does not typecheck
evidence: npm run typecheck: test/taxonomy.test.ts:77 TS2322; heterogeneous object-array inference adds an optional undefined signal incompatible with Record<string, TaxonomyAnswer>. Runtime test passed, compiler gate correctly refused.
